title: Price parsing accepts Infinity, exponent forms and sub-cent values that the page and the request then mishandle
evidence: Line 18 uses Number(); line 19 only tests `price > 0`. Number("Infinity") and Number("1e999") are Infinity, which passes. JSON.stringify(Infinity) is null, so the request body carries `"price":null`. Number("0.001") passes too; line 8/11 show it as 0.00. Traced.
failing_case: Enter price 1e999: the line is added, the list shows 'Infinity' and the total 'Infinity'; Send posts price null. Enter price 0.004: the list and total show 0.00 but the invoice sends 0.004.
remediation: Parse price with one validator: finite, a decimal with at most two places, bounded. Store money as integer cents.

title: Send guard is a 1-second timer, not an in-flight lock: a slow request can be sent twice
evidence: guards.js:21-26 only compares Date.now() with the last click. app.js:24-29 never disables the button while the fetch is pending and never clears or locks `lines`. Traced.
failing_case: Slow network: the POST to /api/invoices takes 3 s. The user clicks Send at t=0 and again at t=1.5 s (nothing on screen has changed). tooSoon() returns false the second time, so a second POST goes out with the same lines. Two invoices are created for one set of lines. Also: lastSend is set before the request, so after a failed send a retry inside 1 s is dropped silently.
remediation: Disable the button (or hold an `inFlight` flag) from click until the response settles, and send an idempotency key with the request so the server can reject a repeat.

title: A successful send shows nothing, and the lines stay in the list, inviting a second send
evidence: app.js:27-28: the failure path alerts, the success path only increments `sentCount`, which is never read (grep: only declared at line 3 and incremented here). No message, no clearing of `lines`, no re-render. Index.html has no status region. WCAG 4.1.3 (AA) status messages. Traced.
failing_case: User adds two lines and clicks Send invoice. The request succeeds. The page looks exactly as before: same lines, same total. The user cannot tell whether it worked, clicks again after a second (tooSoon allows it), and a duplicate invoice is created.
remediation: On success, clear `lines`, re-render, and show a visible, announced status (role=status) such as 'Invoice sent (3 lines, 42.00)'. Remove or use `sentCount`.

title: Draft invoice lines live only in memory and are lost on refresh or close
evidence: No storage, no beforeunload or pagehide handler anywhere in the four files. Traced.
failing_case: User enters 15 lines, accidentally refreshes or closes the tab: all lines are gone with no warning.
remediation: Persist `lines` (versioned, guarded load) to sessionStorage or the server, or warn on unload while the draft is non-empty.

quote: const total = lines.reduce((sum, l) => sum + l.qty * l.price, 0);
title: Invoice total is computed in float arithmetic inside render, and rounded only for display
evidence: app.js:10-11: floating-point sum of qty*price, formatted with toFixed(2) only at the end, while each row is rounded separately (line 8). The pricing rule lives in the view function. Traced arithmetic.
failing_case: Three lines of price 1.005 qty 1 are shown as 1.00, 1.00, 1.00 but the total is shown as 3.01 (float sum 3.0149999...), so the visible rows do not add up to the total. The totals the user sees and any total the server computes can differ by a cent.
remediation: Store integer cents, move the total into one pure, tested function, and have render only display its result.

title: Invalid quantity or price is rejected silently
evidence: app.js:19 returns with no message, no focus move, no aria-invalid. index.html:16 and 18 have no required, no error text. Only the client field has the native `required`. Traced.
failing_case: User types quantity 1.5 (or 0, or blank) or price abc and clicks Add line. Nothing is added and nothing is said.
remediation: Show an inline error tied to the field (aria-describedby, aria-invalid) such as 'Quantity must be a whole number of 1 or more', and move focus to the first bad field.

title: A whitespace-only client passes the required check and is stored as an empty name
evidence: index.html:14 uses `required`, which accepts "   " (non-empty). app.js:16 trims it to ""; app.js:19 never checks `client`. Traced.
failing_case: Type three spaces in Client, 2 and 5.00, Add line: a line with client "" is pushed; the list shows an empty link text ': 2 × 5.00' and the invoice is sent with no client.
remediation: Reject an empty trimmed client in the same validation step as qty and price, with a visible error.

title: Send invoice works with no lines and posts an empty invoice
evidence: Handler at app.js:24-29 has no check on `lines.length`. index.html:23 renders the button always enabled; the list at index.html:21 has no empty-state text. Traced.
failing_case: First run, nothing entered: click Send invoice. The page POSTs `[]` to /api/invoices. Depending on the server it creates an empty invoice or returns an error shown as 'The invoice was not sent. Try again.', which tells the user to retry something that can never work.
remediation: Disable Send while `lines` is empty, and show an empty-state line ('No lines yet. Add a client, quantity and unit price.') in the list.

quote: const res = await fetch("/api/invoices", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify(lines) });
title: Network failure on send or void is not handled: no message, rejected promise
evidence: app.js:26 and 33: fetch is awaited with no try/catch. Only `!res.ok` is handled. When offline, fetch rejects with TypeError, the async handler throws, and the code at lines 27-28 never runs. Traced.
failing_case: User goes offline (or the server is unreachable) and clicks Send invoice. fetch rejects; the only trace is an 'Uncaught (in promise) TypeError' in the console. No alert, no status. The user cannot tell it failed. The same happens for Void at line 33.
remediation: Wrap each request in try/catch and report the cause and next step ('No connection. Your lines are kept; try again.') through one shared error display.

title: JSON body is sent without a Content-Type header, so it goes as text/plain
evidence: fetch with a string body defaults to Content-Type: text/plain;charset=UTF-8. No headers option on app.js:26. The server is not in the payload, so the parsing side is inferred.
failing_case: A server that parses JSON by content type (for example express.json()) ignores the body: req.body is empty, so the invoice is created empty or rejected with 400 even though the lines were valid.
remediation: Add headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" } to both requests, and cover the request shape with a test against the real handler.

title: Void invoice is always visible and enabled but silently does nothing for this user
evidence: app.js:2 hard-codes roles ["viewer","billing"]; guards.js:11 requires "admin". So canVoid(user) is false on every click and the handler returns with no message. index.html:24 renders the button as a normal enabled button. Traced.
failing_case: Signed-in user 'sam' clicks Void invoice. No request, no alert, no change. The button looks broken; there is no hint that admin rights are needed.
remediation: Hide or disable the button (with aria-disabled and an explanation) when the user lacks the role, or show 'Only admins can void an invoice.' on click.

title: Void sends no invoice id, asks no confirmation, and reports no success
evidence: app.js:31-35: no confirm step, no body or id in the request, only the failure path alerts. Nothing on the page says which invoice is current. Traced.
failing_case: An admin clicks Void invoice by mistake (it sits directly beside Send invoice). The POST goes out at once with no way to say which invoice it targets, and no undo. If it succeeds the page shows nothing, so the admin cannot tell whether the invoice was voided.
remediation: Send the invoice id, ask 'Void invoice INV-123? This cannot be undone.' first, and show a visible, announced result.

title: Void permission is checked only in the browser, on a global the user can edit
evidence: canVoid reads the page-global `user` (app.js:2, a `const` at script top level, readable from the console as `user`; the roles array is mutable). The request at app.js:33 carries no identity or invoice id, so the server cannot tell the client's claim from fact. The server is not in the payload; enforcement there is inferred as absent from what the client sends.
failing_case: In the console run `user.roles.push('admin')`, click Void invoice: the guard passes and the POST goes out. If the server relies on the client check, any viewer can void invoices.
remediation: Enforce the admin check on the server from the session, never from client state; keep the client check only to hide or disable the button.

title: Every row's client name is a link to '#' that does nothing but jump to the top
evidence: app.js:8: `<a href="#">` with no handler anywhere. It adds one tab stop per line and a pointless title that repeats the text. Traced.
failing_case: Keyboard user tabs through 10 lines and lands on 10 'links' that each scroll the page to the top and add '#' to the URL.
remediation: Render the client as plain text in the <li>, and drop the duplicate title.

title: The whole list is a live region that is rebuilt on every add, so screen readers re-read old lines
evidence: app.js:7 sets `innerHTML` for the whole list on each render, replacing every <li> inside an aria-live region. Many screen readers announce all of the replaced nodes. Traced from code; no screen reader was run.
failing_case: With 8 lines already listed, adding a 9th causes the reader to announce all 9 rows again instead of just the new one.
remediation: Drop aria-live from the list and announce one short status ('Line added: Acme, 2 × 5.00; total 10.00') in a separate role=status element.

title: Destructive Void sits directly beside the primary Send with identical styling
evidence: index.html:23-24 and styles.css:4: both buttons get the same single `button` rule; no primary/secondary/danger distinction, no spacing between them.
failing_case: On a phone a user aiming for Send invoice hits the adjacent Void invoice, which is the same size and colour.
remediation: Style Send as the one primary action, give Void a distinct danger style, separate them, and add the confirmation step.
